item.title: Can LLMs model real-world systems in TLA+?
item.description:
📝 The invariant phase checks whether the spec satisfies key safety and liveness properties. But, once evaluation reaches the conformance phase, two systematic forms of “textbook modeling” become apparent: (1) the spec enters states that a real system can never reach, and (2) the spec fails to reach states that a real system always reaches. In the cases where the spec enters states the real-world systems never reach, the LLMs write the spec following a common formalization template that does not match the system’s actual data structure, and as a result, the spec admits transitions that produce states that real systems would never produce.
🔗 Read more: https://www.sigops.org/2026/can-llms-model-real-world-systems-in-tla/
